question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{6-5x}{x+7}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{6-5x}{x+7}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{6-5y}{y+7}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{6-5y}{y+7} \\ x(y+7) & =6-5y \\ xy+7x & =6-5y \\ xy+5y & =6-7x \\ y(x+5) & =6-7x \\ y & =\frac{6-7x}{x+5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{6-7x}{x+5}.
$$
